story.title: Death Toll Rises to Nine in Thailand School Shooting as 12-Year-Old Girl Dies
story.summary: A 12-year-old girl has died from critical injuries sustained during a school shooting in Nonthaburi province, Thailand, raising the death toll to at least nine. The shooting, which occurred on Friday, involved a 14-year-old assailant who also reportedly killed his grandparents before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School. The shooter is believed to have taken his own life following the attack.

timeline_highlights.title: Teenager Commits Deadly Shooting at School After Killing Grandparents in Thailand
timeline_highlights.summary: A 14-year-old boy in Thailand killed his grandparents before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, resulting in at least eight deaths, including his own. The attack, which occurred just outside Bangkok, left more than 30 others injured. Authorities reported that the boy used a firearm belonging to his grandfather and fired a total of 26 rounds during the incident. The motive for the shooting remains unclear.

explore_lenses.label: What do investigators know about the attack?
explore_lenses.title: Police are piecing together planning and access to the gun
explore_lenses.summary: Investigators have identified evidence suggesting the alleged attacker had access to his grandfather’s legally registered firearm and had shown an interest in firearms before the attack. That evidence has not established a motive or a definitive explanation for the shooting.

claims.text: Police said the 14-year-old allegedly fired at least 26 rounds from a gun belonging to his grandfather and had 34 additional rounds; investigators also reported finding a knife, spent casings and a personal computer.
Police said a teacher had confiscated an air gun from the boy last year, and that witness accounts indicated he had been interested in learning about firearms for roughly one to two years.
Forensic officials said the gunshot injury found on the alleged shooter was consistent with the weapon used, while more detailed findings, including toxicology, were still pending.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the girl’s death matter now?
explore_lenses.title: The crisis remains acute for injured students and families
explore_lenses.summary: The girl’s death raises the reported toll to nine and underscores that many survivors still require hospital care. The school has paused classes, while families and local residents face immediate trauma and disruption.

claims.text: Police said the 12-year-old died after treatment for critical wounds, raising the death toll to nine; 14 people remained hospitalized, including seven in critical condition.
Thailand’s Health Ministry reported that many of the wounded were ages 12 to 14, making the continuing medical situation especially significant for the school community.
Debsirin Nonthaburi School said it would suspend classes from August 10 through August 14 and have staff work from home.

story_report.summary: A 12-year-old girl has died from injuries suffered in a school shooting in Thailand, bringing the death toll to at least nine, police said. Five school staff members are among those killed. The girl’s death followed treatment for critical wounds, while 14 other people remained hospitalized, including seven in critical condition. The continuing medical toll has prompted Debsirin Nonthaburi School to suspend classes for five days and shift staff to remote work.

sections.heading: Police Investigation of the Teenager
sections.body: Authorities said the alleged shooter was 14 years old and had also killed his grandparents. Police said he fired at least 26 rounds from a gun belonging to his grandfather and had 34 additional rounds; investigators reported finding a knife, spent casings and a personal computer. A teacher had confiscated an air gun from the boy last year, police said, and witnesses described an interest in firearms over roughly one to two years.

sections.heading: Hospital Care and School Closure
sections.body: Many of those wounded were between 12 and 14 years old, according to Thailand’s Health Ministry. Fourteen people remained in hospital after the girl’s death, with seven listed in critical condition. Debsirin Nonthaburi School said classes would be suspended from Aug. 10 through Aug. 14, while staff work from home.

unresolved.text: Authorities had not publicly established a motive. The conditions of the remaining critically injured patients, and whether the death toll will rise further, were also unresolved; detailed forensic findings, including toxicology, were pending.

related_stories.title: Japan Commemorates 81st Anniversary of Nagasaki Atomic Bombing
related_stories.summary: On the 81st anniversary of the atomic bombing of Nagasaki, Mayor Shiro Suzuki condemned the increasing global support for nuclear deterrence, asserting that 'humanity and nuclear weapons cannot coexist.' He labeled nuclear weapons as 'absolute evil' and urged the Japanese government to uphold its non-nuclear principles established after World War II.

related_stories.title: Daniel Kinahan Extradited to Ireland on Government Jet
related_stories.summary: Daniel Kinahan, an alleged crime boss, is being extradited from Dubai to Ireland aboard an Irish government jet. The jet is currently en route to Dublin following his extradition. A high-security operation is in place, including a bulletproof and bombproof van prepared for his transport to court upon arrival.
